title: Dan Dan Noodles
subtitle: Sichuan noodles with spiced pork and peanut sauce
excerpt: Dan dan noodles are a Sichuan street food classic. Wheat noodles are topped with crispy spiced pork mince and a rich peanut and chilli sauce. The dish is fast to make and full of contrasting textures. Mix it all together at the table before eating.
sourceNotes: Dan dan noodles are a Sichuan street food, originally sold by hawkers who carried their equipment on a shoulder pole (dan dan). The dish combines wheat noodles with a spiced minced pork sauce, preserved vegetables, and a sesame-peanut dressing. It has become one of the most widely recognised dishes in Sichuan cuisine.

content.text: Dan dan noodles come together in two parallel tracks: cook the pork in one pan while the noodles boil in a pot. The sauce is made cold in a bowl. Reserve a cup of noodle cooking water before draining -- it loosens the sauce perfectly.

items.prepNote: use 400g wheat noodles, udon, or ramen noodles
use chilli oil and rice wine vinegar mixed -- or just chilli oil

content.text: Mix the peanut butter, soy sauce, chilli oil or chilli flakes, and a splash of stock in a bowl until smooth. This is the sauce base.
Heat oil in a frying pan over high heat. Add the pork mince with garlic and ginger. Stir-fry until browned and slightly crisp -- about 5 minutes.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions. Drain, reserving a cup of cooking water.
Add a splash of cooking water to the sauce to loosen it to a pourable consistency.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Spoon the sauce over. Top with the pork mince and spring onion.
Mix at the table before eating.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and pasty
items.fix: Add the hot noodle cooking water gradually, stirring, until the sauce is pourable. Warm chicken stock also works. The sauce should coat the noodles, not sit in a lump.

content.text: Dan dan noodles were originally a Chengdu street food. Hawkers carried hot broth and noodles through the streets on shoulder poles. Today the dish is served in noodle shops across China and abroad. The balance of peanut, chilli, and soy is the defining characteristic.
